title: Harris-Benedict Energy Expenditure
sources: Harris JA, Benedict FG. PNAS 1918 (original equation); ASPEN/SCCM 2016 critical care nutrition guideline

changelog.change: Switched to the original 1918 Harris-Benedict coefficients per Calculator_Logic_Build_Spec.md (matches MDCalc); prior draft used the Roza-Shizgal 1984 revision.

purpose: Estimates basal energy expenditure (kcal/day) to set an initial nutrition target when indirect calorimetry is unavailable. Multiply by an activity/stress factor for total energy expenditure. Predictive equations are imprecise in critical illness — reassess against weight trend, nitrogen balance, and tolerance.

interpretation.label: Use as a STARTING target only. ASPEN/SCCM: 25–30 kcal/kg/day and 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day protein for most critically ill adults; consider trophic feeding early in ARDS. Avoid overfeeding (hyperglycaemia, hepatic steatosis, raised CO2, refeeding). Titrate to calorimetry, weight, and metabolic tolerance

notes: Common stress factors: minor surgery ~1.2, sepsis / major trauma ~1.3–1.5, major burns up to ~1.5–2.0; add ~1.1–1.2 for fever per °C above normal. In obesity (BMI ≥ 30) use hypocaloric high-protein feeding (11–14 kcal/kg actual or 22–25 kcal/kg ideal body weight). Screen for refeeding risk before starting in the malnourished.
buildNote: Formula engine. Original 1918 Harris-Benedict coefficients (men 66.5 + 13.75·W + 5.003·H − 6.775·A; women 655.1 + 9.563·W + 1.850·H − 4.676·A). sex select folds the male/female equation.
